update_notes.content: Installing or uninstalling the 11.3 version of the Portal for ArcGIS Security 2025 Update 1 Patch may cause the configuration settings for the Web Editor application to be removed, resulting in the application failing to load. This defect is logged as BUG-000176348. During the install and uninstall of a Portal for ArcGIS patch, application settings are repopulated and this defect is the result of a timing problem during that sequence of repopulating application settings. This defect only affects the Web Editor application for version 11.3; starting at version 11.4, the Web Editor application is embedded with Portal for ArcGIS and this timing issue is avoided. To workaround this problem, the Web Editor application should be uninstalled and reinstalled which will reconfigure the application’s settings. While previous workaround notes provided steps to edit the configuration files for the missing values, that manual approach is tedious and error prone and may not be comprehensive because multiple files may have been impacted. The Portal for ArcGIS Security 2025 Update 2 Patch, released May 28, 2025, provides a resolution to avoid this problem when installing a Portal for ArcGIS patch. Please be advised that the application settings are also reconfigured during the uninstall of a Portal for ArcGIS patch and if the Web Editor configuration is impacted by uninstalling the patch, the only resolution will be to uninstall and reinstall the Web Editor application.

update_notes.content: September 24, 2021: An issue has been identified in the ArcGIS Server 10.8.1 Utility Network 5 Patch and the download will be temporarily unavailable. A corrected patch will be available as soon as possible with the necessary updates. The issue discovered has to do with dirty areas not being properly created when edits to associations (connectivity, containment, or structural attachment) made in named versions are reconciled with Default. The result is subsequent validates in Default do not add the association information into the network index. If you have made association edits in your data using ArcGIS Server 10.8.1 Utility Network 5 Patch and reconciled or posted those update to Default, the easiest resolution to the problem is to disable your network topology, and then re-enable it. If your association edits are minimal, the problem could also be addressed by dropping and readding the associations in Default and then running Validate on those changes. Thank you for your patience while a corrected patch is prepared.

Update the MaritimeServer.soe Now that you have updated your configuration files for each map service with MCS enabled, you will need to upgrade your ArcGIS Server Site’s MaritimeServer.soe. Step 1: Login as a Server Manager by launching https://localhost:6443/arcgis/manager. Step 2: Click Site. Step 3: Click Extensions. Step 4: Click Edit Extension under Action. Step 5: Click Choose File and browse to the MaritimeService.soe file located in <ArcGIS Install Directory>\MaritimeServer\Server<version>\Bin Step 6: Click Save. update_notes.content: After the Portal for ArcGIS 11.5 Web Applications Patch is installed on the portal machine, the Web browser cache must be cleared on all machines where the problem of loading an application occurred. Typically when a browser experiences an error, once new files are available, the browser will utilize the new files and overcome the failure. BUG-000177808 causes an unusual and difficult condition where the web application received 0-byte files which resulted in a failure in the web application loading process. These erroneous 0-byte files were cached within the browser and while the patch includes logic to force the recognition of new, corrected files, browser caching may still be in effect and thus the application does not utilize the newly corrected files. It is therefore required that the browser cache be cleared explicitly after the patch has been applied. Clearing of browser cache is required on all machines that consume or connect to web applications impacted by this defect.

update_notes.content: A new version of the ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 Utility Network and Data Management Patch 8 has been released to resolve a problem where registration and validation of a data store fails using ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 on Linux. The defect that is resolved in the new patch is: BUG-000178148 - After installing ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 Utility Network and Data Management Patch 8, registration and validation of a data store fails using ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 on Linux. The patch with a resolution for BUG-000178148 is identified as ArcGIS Server 10.9.1 Utility Network and Data Management Patch 8 B and is listed in the ArcGIS Enterprise Patch Notification tool with a date of August 4, 2025. The B version of the patch can be installed on its own or installed on a deployment where the initial A version is installed; there is no need to uninstall the initial A version. While there is a B version for both Windows and Linux due to how patches are built, BUG-000178148 only impacted Linux.
